currentCoordinate.coordNote: The applied coordinate is the deterministic half-length point of the named Olafiagangen pedestrian geometry. Municipal sources define Olafiagangen under Nylandsbrua and the immediately connected Grønland T underpasses as a finite public-space corridor, replacing the former diffuse editorial proxy.

previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The old point was explicitly retained only as an unsupported editorial proxy. The named Olafiagangen geometry, official place-name identity and municipal under-bridge scope now provide a finite source-backed representation.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The Olafiagangen pedestrian and public-space corridor directly under/along Nylandsbrua between Grønland torg and Akerselva, together with the immediately connected western Grønland T underpass/entrance transition zone.
identity.identityProblem: The editorial title is broader than one mapped object, while graffiti surfaces are transient. Verification therefore requires a stable named public-space spine plus a finite set of connected transit anchors rather than a claimed centroid of all changing walls and passages in Grønland/Vaterland.
identity.splitReason: Municipal sources treat Olafiagangen, the underside of Nylandsbrua and the connected Grønland T underpass/entrance zone as one coherent public-space transition. Individual graffiti surfaces remain transient content rather than separate canonical places.

reproducible line geometry and midpoint derivation

evidence.finding: Oslo kommune describes Olafiagangen as a public passage and meeting place between Grønland torg and Akerselva directly under Nylandsbrua. Bymiljøetaten and Bydel Gamle Oslo manage and upgrade the area, including the underside of Nylandsbrua and the route toward the T-bane entrance.
evidence.reason: Defines the physical and operational scope; map geometry supplies the coordinate.

evidence.sourceName: Bydel Gamle Oslo – SuperGrønland and 2024 district resolution
evidence.finding: Municipal material identifies Olafiagangen as an approximately 5000-square-metre urban space between Grønland torg and Akerselva directly under Nylandsbrua. The district resolution explicitly includes areas under Nylandsbrua and the underpasses to Grønland T in the same physical improvement zone.
evidence.reason: Resolves the previously diffuse editorial scope into a finite public-space and transit-transition environment.

evidence.finding: The named pedestrian way is approximately 89.8 metres long. Its deterministic half-length point is 59.912904676848626, 10.758921861315992, approximately 83.2 metres west of the former editorial proxy.
evidence.reason: Provides the stable named physical spine and reproducible applied point for the finite corridor.

evidence.finding: Kartverket returns exactly one active Olafiagangen object, stedsnummer 998056, with adopted Norwegian spelling and MultiLineString geometry matching the same pedestrian corridor.
evidence.reason: Officially confirms the stable named linear identity independently of OSM.

evidence.finding: The named Nylandsbrua bridge polygon is immediately adjacent to/over the mapped Olafiagangen line. The nearest mapped line-to-polygon distance is approximately 7.5 metres; municipal documentation is authoritative for the statement that Olafiagangen lies directly under the bridge.
evidence.reason: Physical bridge-context cross-check, not the canonical pedestrian coordinate.

evidence.finding: The western Grønland T entrance at 59.9126746, 10.7589679 is approximately 25.7 metres from the applied Olafiagangen midpoint.
The northwest wheelchair-accessible Grønland T entrance at 59.9129856, 10.7586106 is approximately 19.5 metres from the applied midpoint.
evidence.reason: Secondary current transit anchor only; entrance configuration can change during planned station works.

evidence.finding: The previous point 59.9128, 10.7604 was explicitly documented as an unverified editorial midpoint with no stable source object or finite anchor set.
evidence.reason: Replaced now that a finite municipal scope and named geometry are available.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named Olafiagangen line midpoint as the canonical area anchor, retained the western Grønland T entrances as secondary current-access anchors and narrowed the canonical scope to the municipal Olafiagangen/Nylandsbrua transition zone. Continue with grunerlokka_bakgardsvegger.

notes: The canonical point moves approximately 83.2 metres west from an unsupported editorial proxy to the named Olafiagangen geometry.
The radius decreases from 210 to 130 metres because the previously diffuse neighbourhood scope is now resolved to a finite public-space corridor and connected transit entrances.
Transient graffiti surfaces are content evidence, not coordinate sources.
Nylandsbrua is physical overhead context and not the accessible canonical marker.
Current subway entrance nodes are secondary anchors because planned station changes may alter them.
